answers: Bill Cosby was labeled a "violent sexual predator" by the judge who sentenced him to three to 10 years in prison on Tuesday, but his publicist had a different description: one of the "greatest civil rights leaders" in history and one of the "greatest educators of men and boys." Outside the courtroom in Norristown, Pa., publicist Andrew Wyatt claimed the 81-year-old Cosby had faced the "most racist and sexist trial" in American history, the New York Times reports. Wyatt claimed that three psychologists who testified against Cosby in the sexual assault trial were trying to "make money off of accusing black men of being sexual predators." He also read a statement from Camille Cosby, the disgraced entertainer's wife, alleging that an audio recording played in the trial had been doctored. Wyatt, who previously called Cosby's trial a "public lynching," accused Judge Steven O'Neill of being part of a "sex war" and linked the sentencing to the treatment of Supreme Court nominee Brett Kavanaugh. Vox reports that the strangest moment came when Wyatt likened his client to Jesus. "They persecuted Jesus, and look what happened," he said. "Not saying Mr. Cosby is Jesus, but we know what this country has done to black men for centuries." Cosby, who left the Montgomery County Courthouse in handcuffs, spent his first night behind bars at SCI Phoenix, a state prison that opened two months ago in suburban Philadelphia, reports WPVI. (Cosby's mug shot was released Tuesday afternoon.)

full.prediction:
**Summary of News Passages:**

On September 25, 2018, Bill Cosby was sentenced to three to ten years in prison for drugging and sexually assaulting Andrea Constand at his home in 2004. The sentencing, delivered by Judge Steven T. O’Neill, also classified Cosby as a “sexually violent predator,” requiring him to receive monthly counseling for the rest of his life. Cosby, 81, was taken into custody in handcuffs and sent to SCI Phoenix, a new 3,830-bed state prison in suburban Philadelphia, where he will serve his sentence. He is being housed in a single cell near the infirmary and will have access to phone calls, visitation, and exercise during the classification process. His legal team has argued that he should be placed in a facility better suited for his age and medical needs, such as SCI Laurel Highlands, a prison for lower-risk inmates with special care units.

Following the sentencing, Cosby’s publicist, Andrew Wyatt, made strong public statements outside the courthouse, accusing the trial of being “the most racist and sexist trial in the history of the United States.” Wyatt framed Cosby’s conviction as part of a broader “sex war” in Washington, drawing parallels to the controversy surrounding Supreme Court nominee Brett Kavanaugh, who has faced allegations of sexual misconduct from multiple women. Wyatt also claimed that the audio evidence presented in the trial was falsified and criticized the psychologists who testified against Cosby. In a controversial moment, he compared Cosby’s situation to the persecution of Jesus, suggesting that the country has a long history of targeting black men.

Wyatt and other members of Cosby’s legal team have repeatedly invoked historical injustices, such as the case of Emmett Till, to argue that racism played a role in Cosby’s conviction. However, despite these claims, the legal system proceeded with the sentencing, and Cosby’s case has been widely seen as a landmark moment in the #MeToo movement. Meanwhile, the controversy surrounding Kavanaugh continues, with additional accusers coming forward and calls for an FBI investigation, though his confirmation remains likely. Cosby’s case has sparked national debate about justice, accountability, and the intersection of race and gender in legal proceedings.
